title: Ask Distillation Mechanism & Sprint Seedbook — Customer Signals (Nov 2025)
executive_summary: This note captures a compact, repeatable 'ask distillation' approach we piloted with five enterprise accounts (marketing, search, support automation, knowledge embeddings). The goal: convert noisy customer threads into three levels — (A) immediate micro-patches, (B) sprintable features (2–6 weeks), (C) research/ops projects (quarter+). Below are raw signals, cluster insights, prioritized candidates with impact/cost heuristics, and a short seed list for the next two sprints. This is a working artifact meant to seed planning with Product and Eng (SRE/Runtime).
distillation_methodology: 1) Ingest: aggregated transcripts, support tickets, Slack threads, and partner review decks (last 90 days).
2) Tagging: quick pass tags applied by CS reps (latency, cost, accuracy, onboarding, security, KV-cache, model-degradation).
3) Weighting: apply micro-weights — frequency * customer_tier * operational_severity = signal score.
4) Synthesis: cluster into 'user intent' + 'pain vector' then map to implementation lanes (quick-patch, feature, ops).
5) Sanity check: validate high-scoring items with 2 customer contacts before committing to dev time.
raw_signals: Search customers report hallucination spikes when context > 2048 tokens (esp. multi-doc KB retrieval).
Two customers observed 2x token cost after recent quantized model switch; unclear batching/kv-cache behavior.
Frequent ask: ability to pin a fallback model per route (customer wants deterministic fallback with own cost profile).
Support automation: rule-based overrides are brittle when generation deviates; need confidence scores surfaced.
Observability: customers ask for per-request prompt snapshots + model-version used in console exports for audits.
Private deploy customers: want simplified upgrade testing harness for model rollouts (canary simulation w/ shadow traffic).
Embedding customers: inconsistent cosine distributions after quantized/FP16 builds — downstream retrain pain.
clusters_and_insights: Latent-cost regressions: several signals point to workload-sensitive cost changes post-model-variant switches; root cause often batching & kv-cache miss patterns.
Operational auditability: enterprise buyers consistently need exportable evidence (prompt + model + tokens) for compliance.
Fallback/friction: absence of route-level fallback policies results in manual ops during capacity events. Customers prefer declarative fallback rules.
Determinism vs freshness tradeoffs: customers want to pin deterministic, slightly older model for critical flows while using newer models for exploratory features.
Observability blindspots: latency percentiles and per-token breakdowns exist, but customers need correlation by 'prompt shard' (e.g., user profile length, retrieval result size).
prioritized_candidate_features: A1 — Route-level fallback policies (impact: high, dev estimate: 2 sprint days): Declarative config to route to fallback model/region on latency/capacity thresholds. Low infra risk; improves availability for critical routes.
A2 — Per-request audit export (impact: high for enterprise, dev estimate: 2–3 weeks): Bundled export with prompt snapshot, model id, token counts, and timestamp. Required for compliance reviews.

B1 — KV-cache hit/eviction dashboard (impact: medium, dev estimate: 3–4 weeks): Visualize prefix hit rates, common evicted keys, and per-model eviction causes. Helps customers tune caching and reduces token costs.

B2 — Canary harness for private deployments (impact: medium-high, dev estimate: 4–6 weeks): Lightweight simulation runner to shadow traffic and report regressions (latency/cost/quality). Important for on-prem upgrades.

C1 — Confidence scoring + structured signals (impact: medium, research effort): Surface model uncertainty per response to enable rule overrides in automation workflows. Requires model infra work and eval definition.
quick_patches_low_risk: QP1: Short-term docs snippet for 'how to pin model versions and expected cost tradeoffs' (owner:Docs, implement by next Monday).
QP2: Add a console checkbox to include 'raw prompt' in exports (opt-in) — small UI + backend flagging change.
QP3: Temporary guidance for Dedicated customers: recommended batch-size and kv-cache TTL presets per model family (copyable config).
engineering_constraints_and_risks: Fallback routing requires metadata alignment across routing layer and model catalog (model compatibility matrix needed).
Per-request audit export increases storage and retention considerations (GDPR/CCPA) — need policy for sensitive data scrubbing.
KV-cache dashboard depends on existing telemetry; some edge GPUs hide eviction reasons — may need runtime probes.
Confidence scoring entails changes to model response shape for hosted models; could affect existing SDKs/backwards compatibility.
sample_customer_vignettes: Vignette: Large retailer 'DeltaMart' — uses multi-doc retrieval + chat for product lookup. Noticed 3x cost for long queries after recent model change. Pain: cost unpredictability causes budget alarms. Wants: recommended quantization + cache presets per workload.
Vignette: Health org 'ClinFlow' — must export prompt + model id for audits. Current console truncates prompts; asks for full export and retention options with redaction.
Vignette: Search frontend 'Queryly' — experiences rare but severe latency p99 spikes in region eu-west during bulk scoring. Wants per-route fallback to lower-latency region or different model.
open_questions: Q1: What retention period is acceptable for per-request exports for enterprise customers without triggering policy conflicts?
Q2: Can runtime safely expose a stable confidence scalar for all curated models, or is this model-by-model?
Q3: How much engineering effort is acceptable for a KV-cache diagnostics dashboard in the next two sprints? (trade: visibility vs. time-to-market).
proposed_next_steps: 1) Quick sync (30m) with Product (Optimize + Hosted API) and Serving Runtime to align on A1/A2 feasibility (do this week).
2) Ship QP1 & QP3 as documentation + recommended configs (owner: CS + Docs) — target: 7 days.
3) Run signal validation calls with 2 customers per high-score ask before allocating dev tickets (owner: CS reps).
4) Kick small spike for fallback routing: prototype rule format and simulate takeovers in staging (owner: Eng Routing, 1 week).
5) Add A2 to product backlog with compliance owner; include opt-in flag for prompt exports and a default scrubbing pipeline.
notes_to_product_ops: - When framing A1 for PM review, include 2-3 customer quotes and a cost-avoidance estimate (example: DeltaMart's $X/mo).
- Recommend triage matrix: if signal_score > 80 AND at least one enterprise account affected -> prioritize as A.
- For canary harness (B2), list minimum telemetry requirements: latency p50/p95/p99, token counts, model_id, kv_cache_hit_rate.
